correctness.rationale: The Euclidean dot product divided by the positive chord factors is cos(s−r)−q cos(2t+s+r), so the acute probability is one minus three times the fixed-label obtuse probability. For uniform angle the conditional probability at common phase v is (1−arccos(q cos v)/π)², giving the stated dilogarithm and quadratic term. The normalized one-point density has coefficients −(α/2)cos 2t and α(α−2)cos 4t/16. The pure quadratic density contribution integrates to zero: after rotation averaging, the three pair harmonics cos 4s, cos 4r, cos 4(s−r) all integrate to zero on |s−r|>π/2. The boundary term is the integral of α cos(s+r)/4 along each of s−r=±π/2 in the free coordinate, with unit normal delta factor in that coordinate; each cosine integral is −1, giving −α/(2π²). For the analytic remainder use h=(s+r)/2, d=s−r: the moving threshold is |d|>arccos(q cos(2t+2h)), and the triangular domain has |d|<2 min(h,π−h). The two endpoints in h solve transverse analytic equations at h=π/4 and 3π/4. They remain analytic uniformly in t near q=0. Rescaling the resulting integration intervals gives analytic probability; axis exchange gives evenness. Thus the Oα(q⁴) error and both strict local extrema for α≠1 follow. At α=1 only the quadratic cancellation is proved.
residual_risks: Fixed α and local in q; no uniform-in-α estimate, global ordering or quartic sign at α=1 is asserted.

value.rationale: This gives a usable, exact sensitivity of a natural geometric statistic to the joint choice of shape and boundary measure. In particular the two effects cancel exactly for Euclidean arclength and the circle changes from a strict local maximum to a strict local minimum across the speed exponent. That distinction cannot be made using only the known affine-uniform exact law.
